## Overview

Currency Card is a static informational component with a single `displayState` axis covering `show`, `hide`, and `error`. Its structure changes between the complete amount, hidden-value, and error configurations while preserving the flag row and card shell. Color output is semantic and mode-controlled across Light and Dark, and the accessibility extraction finds no interactive focus stops.

**Variant axes.** displayState: error | show | hide (default: show)

### Composition

- _Decorative children: 2 — documented inline in Structure and Color._

## API

_Confidence: high._

> The Figma 'Property' axis is normalized to the engineer-facing displayState enum and selects one mutually exclusive Error, Show, or Hide rendering. The 'Colors semantic' variable collection provides Light and Dark modes; theme selection is automatic and is not a per-instance API property.

| Property | Values | Required | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | ---
| displayState | error, show, hide | optional | show | Mapped from Figma's 'Property' axis; selects the card's Error, Show, or Hide rendering. |
| flag | (string) | optional | 🇬🇧 | Flag or locale marker shown beside the currency code. |
| currencyCode | (string) | optional | GBP | Currency code shown beside the flag. |
| integerPart | (string) | optional | 9,999 | Whole-number portion of the displayed amount. |
| decimalPart | (string) | optional | .99 | Fractional portion of the displayed amount. |

### Example 1 — Show a currency amount

| Property | Value | Notes |
| --- | --- | ---
| displayState | show | Full amount rendering. |
| flag | "🇹🇭" | Thai baht flag marker. |
| currencyCode | "THB" | Currency code. |
| integerPart | "12,345" | Whole-number amount. |
| decimalPart | ".67" | Fractional amount. |

### Example 2 — Hide the currency amount

| Property | Value | Notes |
| --- | --- | ---
| displayState | hide | Uses the design's hidden-value rendering. |

### Example 3 — Error rendering

| Property | Value | Notes |
| --- | --- | ---
| displayState | error | Uses the design's error rendering. |

## Structure

### Anatomy

`text
Currency Card (component set · 849:3263)
├─ Flag Row (frame · 852:139) · decorative
│  ├─ Flag (text)
│  └─ Currency Code (text)
└─ THB Value Container (frame · 852:142) · decorative
   ├─ Integer Part (text)
   └─ Decimal Part (text)
`

_Confidence: high._ _Reconciliation: 1 auto-fixed, 0 retried, 0 unresolved._

> The Figma Property axis is a structural variant axis and is normalized to the API name displayState with error, show, and hide values. Because the child tree changes across these values, each configuration has its own dimensional section. Show is the default anchor variant; it uses HUG sizing, while Error and Hide use the captured fixed 78.3 × 72 frame. All variants share 12 padding, 8 item spacing, 12 corner radius, and a captured strokeWeight of 1 with inside alignment on the card root. Flag Row uses the space-4 (4) token gap; Value Container uses zero item spacing. No sub-components or slots were detected. No Step 3-delta was run because the supplied base JSON contains the required structure evidence and deltaAvailable=false. The compact baseline has no explicit strokes arrays; coverageMatrix therefore applies the specialist R4 stroke-array gate while dimensional border rows retain the captured strokeWeight/strokeAlign values.

## Voice / Screen reader

_Confidence: high._

> - No interactive child or keyboard-navigation container is present in the extracted tree; treat Currency Card as static informational content, omit focusOrder, and do not make the card or its layout frames focusable.
> - Preserve the static reading order: flag, currency code, then amount. Keep Flag Row and THB Value Container structural rather than exposing their FRAME wrappers as extra stops.
> - The Property axis changes displayed value content: show exposes the default 9,999.99 text, hide represents the hidden-value variant, and error exposes only the integer-part child in the extracted variant. No explicit error message or live-region node is present, so do not invent one; if runtime adds one, expose it as a polite live region rather than a focus stop.
> - iOS uses accessibilityElement/children grouping, Android uses mergeDescendants, and Web should prefer native text/group semantics. Do not add button, link, tab, or other interactive roles without implementation evidence.
> - Keep content order stable across states. Do not announce a redundant flag twice if product semantics treat GBP as the complete currency identification; hide the flag from assistive technology only when that redundancy is confirmed.
> - Do not stuff an accessible name with state, value, and error details; use dedicated platform value/state properties when runtime behavior supplies them.
> - Keep the three platform interpretations semantically aligned; do not make this static content focusable on one platform only.

Canonical displayState=error. The extracted variant contains the flag row and only the integer-part child in the value container; no explicit error message or live-region node is present.
